<h2>
                ABOUT
            </h2>
<p>
                Welcome to my page!
            </p>
<p>
                I am a Ph.D. candidate in Political Science at
                The University of Texas at Dallas. I also serve as an Editorial Assistant for <em>Political Analysis</em>, assisting with manuscript processing, reviewer identification, and computational replication checks.
            </p>
<p>
                My research focuses on comparative politics,
                digital politics, and political methodology,
                particularly artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity,
                misinformation, public opinion, and political trust.
            </p>
<p>
                My current research examines how cyber espionage disclosures shape institutional confidence, how citizens assign responsibility for harmful AI systems, and how national AI strategies influence subsequent government policymaking.
            </p>
<p>
                Methodologically, I use causal inference,
                survey experiments, computational social science,
                and quantitative methods.
            </p>
